relevance_note: Single three-generation family in which seven members (P1–P7) carry a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant: 'identified a heterozygous c.2209delC mutation that was present in all members tested'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from hand-written values and checked every span verbatim against the Markdown. No table was transcribed by script: Table 1 (thyroid tests/autoantibodies), Table 2 (HLA typing), Fig. 1 (pedigree) and Fig. 2 (TNFAIP3 analysis) are present only as captions in the Markdown, so their contents (e.g. P2-P4 antibody levels, pedigree, any further relatives) could not be extracted. Notes and possible contradictions: (1) the variant is called 'novel' in the abstract/results, yet the Discussion says its in vitro functional analysis was 'previously reported as a pathogenic mutation (2)' and the family was previously described in ref. 2 (Kadowaki et al.); both recorded. (2) Results say the variant was 'present in all the HT members tested' (P2-P5), while the Discussion says TNFAIP3 was analyzed 'in the present family (P1–P7)' and found 'in all members tested' and that 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20'; I recorded the variant for all seven on the Discussion statement, but whether each of P1, P6 and P7 was individually genotyped is not explicit. (3) HT diagnosis ages (P2 28 yr, P3 27 yr) and tumour diagnosis ages (P4) are recorded in phenotypic_features severity_or_detail rather than in onset or in individual age_at_diagnosis, which I reserved for the HA20 diagnosis (no age given). (4) Ethnicity 'Japanese' rests on the statement that this family was part of a study of nine independent Japanese families. (5) Ages 'currently 6-, 2-, and 1-yr-old, respectively' apply to P1, P6 and P7 in that order; the joint phrase is kept as original text and the ISO field gives each person's age. (6) Inheritance left 'not reported' although P2 (P1's mother) is a carrier, because no parental-testing statement is made (rule 8). (7) Checklist calls kept conservative: 'stomatitis' (P3, P4) not mapped to oral ulcers; bloody stools (P1), possible Crohn's disease (P2) and perineal fistula 'possibly associated with inflammatory bowel disease' (P7) not mapped to GI ulcers/inflammation; Hodgkin lymphoma (P4) not mapped to lymphoproliferation; craniopharyngioma (P4) not mapped to CNS involvement; 'chronic mild hepatitis' (P2) not mapped to autoimmune hepatitis; P2's cervical (subacute necrotizing) lymphadenitis was mapped to lymphadenopathy (observed). Autoimmune thyroiditis is 'excluded' for P1, P6, P7 from the statement naming them as having normal thyroid function and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies (authors add they are too young for this to be apparent); their 'no anti-thyroid autoantibodies' does not exclude the broader autoantibodies item. The HLA haplotype (A*24:02-B*54:01-C*01:02-DRB1*14:03) shared by HT members is HLA typing, not a variant attributed to one person, so it is not recorded in variants. P1's and P6's sex are not stated in the text.
